00006: /**
00007:  * `Buffer` objects are used to represent a fixed-length sequence of bytes. Many
00008:  * Node.js APIs support `Buffer`s.
00009:  *
00010:  * The `Buffer` class is a subclass of JavaScript's [`Uint8Array`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Uint8Array) class and
00011:  * extends it with methods that cover additional use cases. Node.js APIs accept
00012:  * plain [`Uint8Array`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Uint8Array) s wherever `Buffer`s are supported as well.
00013:  *
00014:  * While the `Buffer` class is available within the global scope, it is still
00015:  * recommended to explicitly reference it via an import or require statement.
00016:  *
00017:  * ```js
00018:  * import { Buffer } from 'node:buffer';
00019:  *
00020:  * // Creates a zero-filled Buffer of length 10.
00021:  * const buf1 = Buffer.alloc(10);
00022:  *
00023:  * // Creates a Buffer of length 10,
00024:  * // filled with bytes which all have the value `1`.
00025:  * const buf2 = Buffer.alloc(10, 1);
00026:  *
00027:  * // Creates an uninitialized buffer of length 10.
00028:  * // This is faster than calling Buffer.alloc() but the returned
00029:  * // Buffer instance might contain old data that needs to be
00030:  * // overwritten using fill(), write(), or other functions that fill the Buffer's
00031:  * // contents.
00032:  * const buf3 = Buffer.allocUnsafe(10);
00033:  *
00034:  * // Creates a Buffer containing the bytes [1, 2, 3].
00035:  * const buf4 = Buffer.from([1, 2, 3]);
00036:  *
00037:  * // Creates a Buffer containing the bytes [1, 1, 1, 1] – the entries
00038:  * // are all truncated using `(value &#x26; 255)` to fit into the range 0–255.
00039:  * const buf5 = Buffer.from([257, 257.5, -255, '1']);
00040:  *
00041:  * // Creates a Buffer containing the UTF-8-encoded bytes for the string 'tést':
00042:  * // [0x74, 0xc3, 0xa9, 0x73, 0x74] (in hexadecimal notation)

----- LINHA 1 --------------------------------------------------------------
00001: /**
00002:  * Javascript implementation of PKCS#12.
00003:  *
00004:  * @author Dave Longley
00005:  * @author Stefan Siegl <stesie@brokenpipe.de>
00006:  *
00007:  * Copyright (c) 2010-2014 Digital Bazaar, Inc.
00008:  * Copyright (c) 2012 Stefan Siegl <stesie@brokenpipe.de>
00009:  *
00010:  * The ASN.1 representation of PKCS#12 is as follows
00011:  * (see ftp://ftp.rsasecurity.com/pub/pkcs/pkcs-12/pkcs-12-tc1.pdf for details)
00012:  *
00013:  * PFX ::= SEQUENCE {
00014:  *   version  INTEGER {v3(3)}(v3,...),
00015:  *   authSafe ContentInfo,
00016:  *   macData  MacData OPTIONAL
00017:  * }
00018:  *
00019:  * MacData ::= SEQUENCE {
00020:  *   mac DigestInfo,
00021:  *   macSalt OCTET STRING,
00022:  *   iterations INTEGER DEFAULT 1
00023:  * }
00024:  * Note: The iterations default is for historical reasons and its use is
00025:  * deprecated. A higher value, like 1024, is recommended.
00026:  *
00027:  * DigestInfo is defined in PKCS#7 as follows:
00028:  *
00029:  * DigestInfo ::= SEQUENCE {
00030:  *   digestAlgorithm DigestAlgorithmIdentifier,
00031:  *   digest Digest
00032:  * }
00033:  *
00034:  * DigestAlgorithmIdentifier ::= AlgorithmIdentifier
00035:  *
00036:  * The AlgorithmIdentifier contains an Object Identifier (OID) and parameters
00037:  * for the algorithm, if any. In the case of SHA1 there is none.
00038:  *
00039:  * AlgorithmIdentifer ::= SEQUENCE {
00040:  *    algorithm OBJECT IDENTIFIER,
00041:  *    parameters ANY DEFINED BY algorithm OPTIONAL
00042:  * }

----- LINHA 1 --------------------------------------------------------------
00001: /**
00002:  * A Javascript implementation of Transport Layer Security (TLS).
00003:  *
00004:  * @author Dave Longley
00005:  *
00006:  * Copyright (c) 2009-2014 Digital Bazaar, Inc.
00007:  *
00008:  * The TLS Handshake Protocol involves the following steps:
00009:  *
00010:  * - Exchange hello messages to agree on algorithms, exchange random values,
00011:  * and check for session resumption.
00012:  *
00013:  * - Exchange the necessary cryptographic parameters to allow the client and
00014:  * server to agree on a premaster secret.
00015:  *
00016:  * - Exchange certificates and cryptographic information to allow the client
00017:  * and server to authenticate themselves.
00018:  *
00019:  * - Generate a master secret from the premaster secret and exchanged random
00020:  * values.
00021:  *
00022:  * - Provide security parameters to the record layer.
00023:  *
00024:  * - Allow the client and server to verify that their peer has calculated the
00025:  * same security parameters and that the handshake occurred without tampering
00026:  * by an attacker.
00027:  *
00028:  * Up to 4 different messages may be sent during a key exchange. The server
00029:  * certificate, the server key exchange, the client certificate, and the
00030:  * client key exchange.
00031:  *
00032:  * A typical handshake (from the client's perspective).
00033:  *
00034:  * 1. Client sends ClientHello.
00035:  * 2. Client receives ServerHello.
00036:  * 3. Client receives optional Certificate.
00037:  * 4. Client receives optional ServerKeyExchange.
00038:  * 5. Client receives ServerHelloDone.
00039:  * 6. Client sends optional Certificate.
00040:  * 7. Client sends ClientKeyExchange.
00041:  * 8. Client sends optional CertificateVerify.
00042:  * 9. Client sends ChangeCipherSpec.

00002: 
00003: class LRUCache {
00004:   constructor () {
00005:     this.max = 1000
00006:     this.map = new Map()
00007:   }
00008: 
00009:   get (key) {
00010:     const value = this.map.get(key)
00011:     if (value === undefined) {
00012:       return undefined
00013:     } else {
00014:       // Remove the key from the map and add it to the end
00015:       this.map.delete(key)
00016:       this.map.set(key, value)
00017:       return value
00018:     }
00019:   }
00020: 
00021:   delete (key) {
00022:     return this.map.delete(key)
00023:   }
00024: 
00025:   set (key, value) {
00026:     const deleted = this.delete(key)
00027: 
00028:     if (!deleted && value !== undefined) {
00029:       // If cache is full, delete the least recently used item
00030:       if (this.map.size >= this.max) {
00031:         const firstKey = this.map.keys().next().value
00032:         this.delete(firstKey)
00033:       }
00034: 
00035:       this.map.set(key, value)
00036:     }
00037: 
00038:     return this
00039:   }
00040: }

00012: /**
00013:  * A data structure which is a combination of an array and a set. Adding a new
00014:  * member is O(1), testing for membership is O(1), and finding the index of an
00015:  * element is O(1). Removing elements from the set is not supported. Only
00016:  * strings are supported for membership.
00017:  */
00018: function ArraySet() {
00019:   this._array = [];
00020:   this._set = hasNativeMap ? new Map() : Object.create(null);
00021: }
00022: 
00023: /**
00024:  * Static method for creating ArraySet instances from an existing array.
00025:  */
00026: ArraySet.fromArray = function ArraySet_fromArray(aArray, aAllowDuplicates) {
00027:   var set = new ArraySet();
00028:   for (var i = 0, len = aArray.length; i < len; i++) {
00029:     set.add(aArray[i], aAllowDuplicates);
00030:   }
00031:   return set;
00032: };
00033: 
00034: /**
00035:  * Return how many unique items are in this ArraySet. If duplicates have been
00036:  * added, than those do not count towards the size.
00037:  *
00038:  * @returns Number
00039:  */
00040: ArraySet.prototype.size = function ArraySet_size() {
00041:   return hasNativeMap ? this._set.size : Object.getOwnPropertyNames(this._set).length;

00025:   return `${y}-${m}-${d}`;

00033:   return dt.getUTCFullYear() === y && dt.getUTCMonth() === m - 1 && dt.getUTCDate() === d;

00030: function parseTargetDate(ymd, hour) {
00031:   if (!isYMD(ymd)) return null;
00032:

00038:   const hh = Number(m[1]);
00039:

00041:   return Number.isNaN(dt.getTime()) ? null : dt;
00042: }

00002: 
00003: export function cacheGet(map, key) {
00004:   const entry = map.get(key);
00005:   if (!entry) return null;
00006: 
00007:   const ts = Number(entry?.ts || 0);
00008:   if (!Number.isFinite(ts) || Date.now() - ts > CACHE_TTL_MS) {
00009:     map.delete(key);
00010:     return null;
00011:   }
00012: 
00013:   return entry.data ?? null;
00014: }
00015:

00019:  * Retorna "00" se inválido.

00022:   const s0 = String(g ?? "").trim();

00025:   // 1) se já vier exatamente "07"

00027:     const n = Number(s0);
00028:     if (!Number.isFinite(n) || n < 1 || n > 25) return "00";
00029:     return pad2(n);
00030:   }
00031: 
00032:   // 2) se vier "7"
00033:   if (/^\d{1,2}$/.test(s0)) {
00034:     const n = Number(s0);
00035:     if (!Number.isFinite(n) || n < 1 || n > 25) return "00";
00036:     return pad2(n);
00037:   }
00038: 
00039:   // 3) extrai 1-2 dígitos de dentro do texto (ex.: "Grupo 25", "25 - VACA")
00040:   const m = s0.match(/(\d{1,2})/);
00041:   if (m) {
00042:     const n = Number(m[1]);
